channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: UZCARD Launches Apple Pay for Cardholders in Uzbekistan
item.description: UZCARD has introduced Apple Pay for its cardholders in Uzbekistan, enabling easy, secure, and private contactless payments via iPhone and Apple Watch. Initially, the service is available for UZCARD cards issued by Halk Bank.

item.title: Kazakhstan and USA to Jointly Promote Agricultural Projects
item.description: Kazakhstan's Minister of Agriculture met with the US Ambassador to discuss expanding agricultural trade, attracting investment, developing livestock, and implementing modern agrotechnologies. The US confirmed its readiness to further develop trade and economic ties and cooperation in the agricultural sector.

item.title: Almaty Identifies Main Air Pollution Sources and Emission Reduction Measures
item.description: Road transport accounts for about 60% of Almaty's annual pollutant emissions. Other sources include private homes using coal and wood for heating, and businesses like bathhouses and eateries. Natural factors like temperature inversions also contribute. New environmental rules aim to reduce emissions from stationary sources and transport.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Dollar Exchange Rate Decreases, Central Bank Announces Rates
item.description: The exchange rate of the US dollar against the Uzbek soum has decreased. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has announced the official exchange rates for foreign currencies against the Uzbek soum, effective November 18.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Plan to Increase Regular Flights and Joint Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev met with Omani officials, noting increased trade and setting a goal of $1 billion in bilateral trade. A portfolio of $5 billion in joint projects was formed, focusing on industrial cooperation, transport, tourism, resource development, and digital technologies.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Extending Ban on Timber Exports Outside EAEU
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Economy proposes extending the temporary ban on exporting timber and wood products outside the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The current ban expires in December, and the extension aims to prevent re-export of timber imported from EAEU member states.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Aim to Increase Trade Turnover to $1 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have set a goal to increase mutual trade turnover to $1 billion. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced this at the opening of the Uzbek-Omani business forum in Muscat. A portfolio of joint projects worth $5 billion was formed, focusing on industrial cooperation, transport, tourism, mineral resources, and digital technologies.

item.title: Four Foreign Nationals Arrested in Bishkek for Alleged Online Casino Payment Facilitation
item.description: Four foreign citizens have been arrested in Bishkek on suspicion of organizing illegal financial operations for online casinos. Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that the group used mobile phones with banking applications to process bets and payouts. Police seized 22 phones and three computer devices during the search.

item.title: Epidemiologist Explains How Vaccination Impacts Child Health and Prevents Diseases
item.description: Vaccination plays a crucial role in protecting child health by preventing infectious diseases and reducing the severity of illness. According to an epidemiologist from the Republican Center for Immunoprophylaxis, vaccines help develop immunity, protect individuals, and contribute to community health. Unvaccinated children face higher risks of contracting serious diseases.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Investigate Alleged Sexual Assault in School Toilet
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Kostanay region are investigating an alleged sexual assault of a student in a school toilet. The incident, reported on social media and by the "NeMolchi.kz" foundation, involves two sixth-graders and a fifth-grader. Authorities have confirmed a criminal case has been opened and are urging against premature conclusions while the investigation continues.

item.title: Almaty Approves 2040 Master Plan: Stricter Building Codes and Transport Restrictions Ahead
item.description: Almaty has approved its master plan for development until 2040, introducing significant changes including a ban on buildings taller than three stories in certain areas and restrictions on older vehicles entering the city. The plan aims to increase construction, relocate some industrial sites, and expand road networks, anticipating population growth to 3.6 million by 2040.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Platform to Connect Local Manufacturers with Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched a unified electronic platform, icppa.uz, to foster cooperation between local manufacturers, suppliers, and investors. The platform aims to consolidate information on domestically produced goods, production capacities, and the needs of large investment projects, facilitating greater involvement of local businesses in national development initiatives.

item.title: Uzbekistan Airways Implements New US Travel Rules Due to Ebola Concerns
item.description: Uzbekistan Airways has introduced new entry requirements for passengers traveling to the United States. Starting November 16, 2026, travelers must confirm they have not visited the Democratic Republic of Congo in the past 21 days. These measures, aimed at preventing Ebola spread, are in effect until February 16, 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Opens Digital Offices with AI Assistants in Nine Cities
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched digital offices in nine cities, including Astana and Shymkent, where citizens can access public services using artificial intelligence. These centers feature terminals and workstations connected to digital services, with an AI assistant named eGov GPT to guide users through processes.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Acwa Explore Carbon Credits for Four Wind Farm Projects
item.description: Uzbekistan and Saudi energy firm Acwa are assessing the potential for four wind projects, including the 1.5 GW Kungrad farm in Karakalpakstan, to generate carbon credits. The review follows an MoU signed at COP28, aiming to meet Paris Agreement requirements for international carbon markets.

item.title: New BIGBON Production Line Launched in Alatau, Kazakhstan, Creating Over 100 Jobs
item.description: A new BIGBON instant noodle production line has been launched at the "Mareven Food Tian-Shan" plant in Alatau, Almaty region, Kazakhstan. The facility represents one of the first of its kind in the country and represents an investment of 4.9 billion tenge. The project is expected to create over 100 new jobs for local residents and boost the regional economy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Promises Long-Term Orders for Businesses Adopting Localization and Local Raw Materials
item.description: Kazakh businesses are being offered long-term orders in exchange for increasing localization of production and utilizing domestic raw materials. This initiative aims to stimulate domestic industry and reduce reliance on imports. Companies that commit to these terms will receive guaranteed contracts, fostering growth and stability within the Kazakh economy.

item.title: Kazakh Millionaires to Construct Sunflower Oil Plant Near Ayagoz
item.description: Businessmen Kanat Kopbaev and Aigazy Kusainov plan to build a sunflower oil plant in the Abai region, near Ayagoz. The project will initially occupy 40 hectares, with potential expansion to 80-120 hectares. The facility will focus on deep processing of agricultural raw materials. The regional administration is ready to assist with land allocation and infrastructure.

item.title: All Oil Product Prices Increase Across Kazakhstan
item.description: The price of all types of oil products has risen in Kazakhstan. According to the National Statistics Bureau, the average price per ton of crude oil reached 104,500 tenge in October 2026, an 8.6% increase year-on-year. Prices for gasoline, diesel, fuel oil, and bitumen have also seen significant hikes.

item.title: Kazakhstan-Orenburg Oblast Trade Reaches $641.7 Million
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov met with Orenburg Oblast Governor Yevgeny Solntsev to discuss trade, transport, and industrial cooperation. Bilateral trade increased by 13.7% to $641.7 million in 2025. Kazakhstan and Russia aim to boost mutual trade to $30 billion.

item.title: Kazakhstan Approves New Master Plan for Almaty Through 2040
item.description: The government of Kazakhstan has approved a new master plan for Almaty, projecting the city's development until 2040. The plan forecasts a population increase to 2.75 million by 2030 and 3.6 million by 2040. It also outlines significant new housing construction and prioritizes economic development, including technological advancements and a green economy.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Enhances Care for Premature Infants, Improving Survival Rates
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has significantly improved care for premature newborns, with modern equipment and new treatments like surfactant therapy. The Ministry of Health reports enhanced training for medical staff in resuscitation and intensive care. Annually, around 5,000 babies are born at the National Center for Maternity and Child Welfare, with about 600 premature, including those under 1.5 kg.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Testing Domestic Digital Maps in Qajet Taxi App
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development is exploring the use of domestic digital maps within the Qajet Taxi ride-hailing application. This initiative aims to utilize maps and navigation services developed by the National Centre of Geodesy and Spatial Information. The project could potentially reduce reliance on foreign systems like Russia's 2GIS.

item.title: Perceived Inflation in Uzbekistan Exceeds 10%, Central Bank Reports
item.description: Perceived inflation in Uzbekistan has risen again, reaching 10.2% in October, according to the Central Bank's latest report. This figure is 1% higher than the previous month. Tashkent leads with the highest inflation expectations at 12.1%.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Labor Code Strengthened to Prohibit Workplace Sexual Harassment
item.description: Uzbekistan's President signed amendments to the Labor Code on November 13, officially prohibiting sexual harassment in the workplace. The new article defines sexual harassment and mandates employers to create a harassment-free environment.

item.title: Taliban Leader Akhundzada Granted 'Sheikh al-Islam' Title by Clerics
item.description: Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada has been conferred the title 'Sheikh al-Islam' by religious scholars from across Afghanistan during a gathering at Kabul University. Akhundzada emphasized unity under his leadership and adherence to the Hanafi school of Islam.

item.title: Russia Includes Central Asia in Ukraine Conditions: Implications for Kazakhstan
item.description: Russia has incorporated Central Asia into its conditions regarding Ukraine, raising questions about the implications for Kazakhstan. The specific nature of these conditions and their potential impact on regional dynamics are under scrutiny.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Allow Prisoners to Enroll in Universities Remotely from 2027
item.description: Starting from the 2027/2028 academic year, prisoners in Uzbekistan will be permitted to enroll in higher education institutions and pursue distance learning on a paid contract basis. This initiative is part of the 'New Life' program, aiming to reduce recidivism by 30%.

item.title: Two Former Kazakh Vice-Ministers and Credit Bureau Head Convicted for Sabotage
item.description: Two former vice-ministers and the head of a credit bureau in Almaty, Kazakhstan, have been convicted. They are accused of reducing a state institution's revenue and enabling a private company to earn more, including using a computer virus to hinder a competitor's operations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman Meets with Compatriots in Moscow
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman, Jamilya Jamanbaeva, held a meeting with Kyrgyz citizens in Moscow at the Kyrgyz Embassy. Representatives from Russian human rights bodies, migration services, and Kyrgyz consular staff attended. Many concerns raised related to migration registration and extending stay permits, with some facing deportation risks. Labor rights violations were also discussed.

item.title: Lenovo Opens First Office in Tashkent, Focusing on AI and Business Growth
item.description: Lenovo has officially opened its first local office in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, marking a strategic expansion in Central Asia. The event, attended by over 250 business and IT leaders, highlighted discussions on AI trends, AI-native business, and technology implementation cases. The new office aims to strengthen partnerships and customer engagement.

item.title: South Korea's Hana Bank Accredited to Open Representative Office in Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has accredited South Korea's Hana Bank to open a representative office in the country. The office aims to study the financial market and expand cooperation with state bodies, financial institutions, and the private sector. Hana Bank is a major commercial bank operating in 27 countries worldwide.

item.title: Organizers of Illegal Umrah Trips Detained in Uzbekistan
item.description: Individuals organizing illegal Umrah trips have been detained in Uzbekistan's Andijan and Tashkent regions. In Andijan, a travel firm head was arrested for promising to send three citizens to Saudi Arabia for $3,350. In Tashkent region, a private training center head was detained for demanding $4,800 for a similar illegal service.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sets $65 Billion Foreign Investment Target for 2027
item.description: Uzbekistan aims to attract $65 billion in foreign investment by 2027, focusing on manufacturing and major international companies. The government forecasts economic growth of at least 8% in 2026 and 7% in 2027, with GDP expected to exceed $200 billion. Priority sectors include chemicals, machinery, and textiles.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Digital Development Ministry Investigates Potential Supreme Court Database Leak
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Digital Development is investigating a potential leak of a database believed to belong to the Supreme Court. The investigation follows a report from the international company SOCRadar regarding the alleged data breach. No further details have been released at this time.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet Fulfilled Over 3,200 Parliamentary Requests
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet has fulfilled and closed 3,270 out of 3,287 parliamentary requests since the VIII convocation of the Jogorku Kenesh began. The government also received 42 parliamentary resolutions, executing 24 fully. Prime Minister Adylbek Kasymaliev presented these figures, emphasizing parliamentary control as a key area of interaction.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches 125 Industrial Projects to Boost Domestic Manufacturing
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched 125 industrial projects valued at $2 billion since early 2026, with 75 more nearing completion, totaling 200 projects with over $3.8 billion in planned investment. These projects aim to produce $3.4 billion in goods annually, create over 17,000 jobs, and introduce new domestic manufacturing capabilities.

item.title: Eight Districts in Tashkent Get New Prosecutors
item.description: Eight districts in Tashkent have new prosecutors appointed by the Prosecutor General of Uzbekistan. These appointments include Mirabad, Sergeli, Yunusabad, Chilonzor, Yashnabad, Almazar, Mirzo-Ulugbek, and Yakkasaray districts. The press service of the Tashkent prosecutor's office announced the changes.

item.title: US Lawmakers Urge Halt to Afghan Deportations, Citing Risk of Reprisal
item.description: Two US House members urged the Trump administration to halt deportations of Afghans who aided American forces, warning of risks upon return. They emphasized honoring commitments to allies who risked their lives and called for preventing deportations of those seeking refuge.

item.title: Over 170,000 Vehicles Registered in Kazakhstan During October
item.description: In October, Kazakhstan registered 172,200 vehicles, including 153,800 passenger cars. As of November 1, 2026, the total number of registered vehicles in the country reached 6,140,700. Passenger cars constitute 83.9% of the total registered fleet.
